CHAPTER 21  Nutrition in Weight Management
Lipoprotein Lipase
Dietary TG is transported to the liver by chylomicrons. Endog-
enous TGs, synthesized in the liver from free fatty acids (FFA) 
travel as part of very low–density lipoprotein particles. The 
enzyme lipoprotein lipase (LPL) moves lipid from the blood 
into the adipose cell, by hydrolyzing TGs into free fatty acids 
and glycerol. Glycerol proceeds to the liver; fatty acids enter the 
adipocyte and are reesterified into TGs. When needed by other 
cells, TGs are hydrolyzed once again to fatty acids and glycerol 
by hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) within the adipose cell; 
they then are released into the circulation.
Hormones affect LPL activity in different adipose tissue 
regions. Estrogens stimulate LPL activity in the gluteofemoral 
adipocytes, and thus promote fat storage in this area for 
childbearing and lactation. In the presence of sex steroid 
hormones, a normal distribution of body fat exists. With a 
decrease in sex steroid hormones—as occurs with menopause 
or gonadectomy—central obesity tends to develop.
